newsitem.title: JAPAN: Record low turnout likely in Japan election.
newsitem.headline: Record low turnout likely in Japan election.

text.p: Voter turnout for Japan's general elections on Sunday stood at 38.44 percent as of 2 p.m. (0500 GMT), on track to break the record low set in the 1993 polls, the Home Affairs Ministry said.

Turnout for the contest, in which 500 seats in the Lower House of parliament are up for grabs, was 6.9 percentage points below that at the same time in the 1993 elections, which set a record low of 67.26 percent of registered voters, a ministry spokesman told reporters.

Political leaders have described the first general election since 1993 as a "landmark" and "turning point" because it will elect a government to lead Japan for the next four years into the 21st century.
Most media polls have predicted that Prime Minister Ryitaro Hashimoto, 59, will remain at the helm of government after the election if his Liberal Democratic Party captures a clear majority.
On the eve of the election, Hashimoto had pleaded for a big turnout from the 98 million electorate, warning if voters stayed away it could allow opposition parties to gain strength.
The low voter turnout so far, even in the mainly good weather, has cast a cloud over the LDP's hope to return to sole power.
